problem:
A zoo is tracking the number of penguins in a habitat.
They observe that new penguins arrive at a rate $r(t)$ given by the function

$$
r(t)=30{e}^{-t/2},
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in penguins per month, and $t>0$ is the time in months since the tracking began.
At the same time, $3$ penguins are transferred out each month.

If there were initially $200$ penguins in the habitat, find the expression that gives $P(t),$ the number of penguins in the habitat $t$ months after the tracking began.

$P(t)=-60{e}^{-t/2}\,+$

{{field-1}}

feedback.problem:
Engineers are testing a water pump filling a reservoir.
They observe that water enters the reservoir at a rate $r(t)$ given by the function

$$
r(t)=12\sqrt{t+4},
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in gallons per minute, and $t>0$ is the time in minutes since the pump was turned on.
At the same time, water leaks from the reservoir at a constant rate of $6$ gallons per minute.

If the reservoir was initially empty, find the expression that gives $V(t),$ the volume of water in the reservoir $t$ minutes after the pump was turned on.

$V(t)=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,6t-64$
feedback.worked_solution:
Water is entering the reservoir at a rate of $r(t)$ gallons per minute and is leaking at a rate of $6$ gallons per minute. Therefore, the **rate of change** $R(t)$ of the volume of water is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(t) & =r(t)-6 \\  & =12\sqrt{t+4}-6.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the total volume $V(t)$ after $t$ minutes, we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}V(t) & =V(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}R(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}(12\sqrt{x+4}-6)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To ensure that our final function is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration. Also, since the reservoir is initially empty, we set $V(0)=0.$

We can simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V(t) & ={\int }_{0}^{t}12\sqrt{x+4}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{t}6\,\text{d}x \\  & ={12\cdot \frac{2(x+4)^{3/2}}{3}|}_{0}^{t}-6x{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =8(t+4)^{3/2}-8(4)^{3/2}-6t \\  & =8(t+4)^{3/2}-6t-64\end{aligned}
$$
